tablecloth noun

classical

Mart. XIV 138

1The libellī use linteum for the tablecloth (Mart. XIV 138). Traupman (p. 125) gives mantēle, which is a tablecloth only in a post-classical sense (Lewis & Short: Isidore, Orig. 19.26.6; Trebellius Pollio). Ruling: linteum and mantēle.

linteum1

noun, second declension

The libellī use it for the tablecloth.

Other words

  • mantēle, mantēlis n. — tablecloth, in a later sense

    noun, third declension · also used · post-classical · Isidore, Orig. 19.26.6; Trebellius Pollio (Lewis & Short); Traupman 125

    Later also a tablecloth, a post-classical sense, which Traupman gives.

See also napkin, set the table.

SourcesLewis & Short: mantele
